summary:
The base-pin preflight repair worked. Mandatory Mac acceptance at d940aaa then passed fd_inheritance, sigint, sigterm and sighup. Inside hung_supervisor it completed every subcase from hung through wait, including closed_status, which logged an owned-zombie anchor proof with a status-2 row and then two SZOMB=5 rows. It failed at subcase 'unresolved' with PermissionError (errno 1). The traceback ends in Probe.cleanup at test_git_containment.py:1427, which is kernel.absent(self.supervisor.pgid, group=True) -> os.killpg(pgid, 0) in _git_process_identity.absent:169.

Cleanup had already verified the host pin, sent SIGKILL only to the host, recorded the decision before reap and reaped the host (host_absent=true). The supervisor that lost its parent was not yet absent, and killpg(…,0) on its transitional or zombie-only group returned EPERM. The controller's passive absence loop lets PermissionError escape on the first poll instead of treating it as inconclusive and polling until the existing deadline. The production _group_gone and the parent_sigkill probe already treat EPERM that way. The fixture correctly stayed UNRESOLVED with nonempty owned_processes. No containment PASS is implied and none is inherited.

This is a test-controller defect in the allowlisted tools/llmtool/tests/test_git_containment.py. The repair is bounded: production code, thresholds, deadlines and assertions stay unchanged. The other nine scenarios, including both x20 parent-SIGKILL variants, did not run and remain pending. The runner's independent read-only PID-absence check of the retained inventory (host 51572, supervisor/PGID 51573, members 51574/51575) is still required before the next native attempt. No saved ID may be signaled.

findings.detail: Probe.cleanup's passive disappearance loop (lines ~1421-1435) calls kernel.absent() on the host, supervisor, supervisor PGID and members with no PermissionError handling. On Darwin, kill/killpg(…,0) can return EPERM for an exiting or zombie-only group. That happens here after host SIGKILL, when the supervisor reaches EOF, runs its last-act self-group SIGKILL, and is reparented and awaiting launchd reap. The uncaught EPERM aborts cleanup on the first poll, so a transient inspection result becomes a hard failure. Repair guidance: wrap each poll iteration's observations so PermissionError counts as inconclusive. Never treat it as absence. Record a bounded fact such as proof['inspection_eperm']=True or a counter, keep that poll's affected flags False, and continue polling under the SAME existing deadline. Do not extend the 2s F1 or 6s controller bounds. If the deadline expires without positive absence for host, supervisor, group and all members, raise IdentityUnknown('probe group disappearance unconfirmed') with status UNRESOLVED and the probe kept in _FAILED_PROBES. Add no signals: no kill or killpg on supervisor, group or member IDs, and no retry of the host signal. Add deterministic ControllerCleanupTests: (a) transient EPERM followed by ProcessLookupError absence gives RESOLVED with host-only SIGKILL and no group signal; (b) persistent EPERM until the deadline gives UNRESOLVED, the probe retained, and no group signal. Keep test_retained_group_or_inspection_permission_is_not_resolved passing; it already accepts IdentityUnknown. Preserve all other assertions, inventory freezing, the decision-before-reap order and the primary-error retention.
findings.evidence: failure-0.json at mac.failure: scenario hung_supervisor, subcase unresolved, PermissionError errno 1 'Operation not permitted'. The traceback runs main:84 -> hung_supervisor:2074 -> unresolved_exit:2118 -> cleanup_preserving_failure:61 -> resolve_fixture:2113 -> cleanup:1457 -> cleanup:1427 -> _git_process_identity.absent:169. fixture_cleanup.evidence has host_pin_verified/decision_before_reap/host_reaped/host_absent=true, supervisor_absent=false, group_absent=false, members_absent=[], status UNRESOLVED. Line 1427 is kernel.absent(self.supervisor.pgid, group=True). By contrast, _git_containment._group_gone and AcceptanceScenarios.parent_sigkill catch PermissionError as inconclusive, and _git_process_identity.Anchor.kill_group notes 'A zombie-only group may yield EPERM'. The stdout log shows four scenarios passing, then closed_status owned-zombie proof, then 'hung_supervisor FAIL (PermissionError)'.

findings.detail: Process note, not a code change: the repaired candidate must rerun syntax, related checks, ordinary review, both full suites and all fourteen native scenarios on the changed bytes. Before the next native attempt, the outer runner must prove read-only that the retained original inventory is absent: host 51572, supervisor/PGID 51573, members 51574 and 51575. EPERM or retained PIDs block. The runner must not signal saved IDs.
